title: What Is A Rimless Toilet And Are They Better?
bodyHtml:
So what's all this fuss about Rimless Toilets Anyway?

With the popularity of Rimless toilets on the rise, we are often asked what exactly are the differences compared to the traditional toilet technology, aka the "Boxed Rim" design which has been a standard in Australian bathrooms for decades.

In this month's bathroom design talk, we delve into everything you need to know about Rimless toilets; What is a Rimless toilet exactly? What are the benefits of installing a Rimless toilet and of course, are they really a better choice?

What is a Rimless Toilet?

Rimless is the term used to describe the latest flushing technology in toilets where the "Rim" has literally been removed. This differs from the traditional "Box Rim" style which borders the top of a toilet bowl to distribute the flush water evenly, in a downward motion.

A rimless toilet on the other hand actually has the whole bowl exposed to the top edge, and propels water in a vortex like motion around the toilet bowl, usually from the rear, to achieve the same result.

Are Rimless Toilets Actually Better?

Rimless Toilets are the new standard and preferred flushing technology with many manufacturers now leaving box rim design in the past. The short answer is yes, they are better provided the efficiency and efficacy of the flush is well designed, but we'll get more into this in a moment.

Are Rimless Toilets More Hygienic?

The clear advantage of a Rimless toilet design is that it is definitely the more hygienic choice. The removal of the rim means that the entire toilet bowl is exposed unlike the box rim design which creates a hard to reach area where bacteria and grime can manifest without concentrated cleaning.

 

How do I clean a Rimless Toilet?

Cleaning under the rim of a “boxed rim” toilet involves a lot of guesswork and concentrated cleaning. However, the Rimless toilet design makes improved toilet hygiene a breeze.

The removed rim means there are no longer unreachable crevices or corners around the toilet bowl, eliminating opportunities for germs and bacteria to hide. A simple yet often overlooked method of cleaning and removal of any build up or stains is to use white vinegar. Pour a generous amount around the bowl and leave for half an hour, then simply wipe with a cloth or toilet brush. White vinegar also ensures that the surface of your toilet remains in tact and avoids any warranty issues that may arise using harsh cleaning products that may damage the surface of your toilet.

Do Rimless Toilets have a better flush?

Rimless toilets typically have superior flushing performance vs traditional box rim performance, provided the toilet is well designed. A well designed rimless flush uses pressure jets to project water around the bowl, effectively helping to clean the inner bowl's surface as the water moves around the bowl in a vortex like motion, which differs greatly to box rim toilets that propel water in a downwards motion only.

Effectiveness of flush is directly related to how well the toilet's bowl and flushing jets have been engineered. A superior flush design will result in water being propelled higher towards the top of the rim, meaning more water coverage across the inner bowl for the duration of the flush. In cases where Rimless flushing is not covering the majority of the bowl surface with water or the pressure jets are not effectively propelling water with enough pressure to remove build up from the surface during flush, then a traditional box rim design would have a superior flush.

Are Rimless Toilets Noisy?

Another benefit of Rimless toilets is their quieter flush. Depending on the manufacturer, the direct flush system eliminates the need for a flapper valve, which is a major contributor of noise in box rim systems. Additionally, the smooth surface of Rimless toilet bowls helps reduce water turbulence, allowing for a quieter flush.

Do Rimless toilets use more or less water?

This depends on the effectiveness of the individual design, so you'll find Rimless toilets have a range of efficiency much like traditional box rim toilets.

If you're opting for a Rimless toilet to replace your existing suite, then we definitely recommend finding a more water efficient solution than your current setup. In Australia the WELS star rating is the best indicator for water efficiency and you can know exactly how much water is being used per flush through this standard system.

Do Rimless toilets cost more?

Rimless toilets are available at every price point to suit your particular project needs, but the general answer is no. You can get a Rimless toilet for the same price you'd expect a traditional box rim to be, so if you're looking at upgrading your toilet, price is not an affecting factor.

Are there a wide variety of Rimless Toilet Designs?

Yes! Rimless toilets are available in a wide variety of design styles meaning you'll be able to find something to suit your desired aesthetic with ease.

Rimless toilets are also available in all types of configurations, from the standard Back to Wall Suite, to Wall Faced toilets and Wall Hung options where the cistern is concealed behind the wall.

Do Rimless Toilets Splash Up?

A well designed Rimless toilet elimnates splashing regardless of the removal of the rim. There are however instances of minor splashback in Rimless toilets due to the lack of rim to conceal the water flow, however, this would be caused by poor design and engineering or caused by incorrect installation. We would recommend to flush test a rimless toilet before purchase to see if splashback may be problematic.

What are the cons of Rimless toilet design?

The major considerations you need to be aware of with Rimless toilet technology is the effectiveness of the flush in regards to how well the bowl is cleaned, and the possibility of water splashing now that the Rim has been removed.

While Australian toilets must pass specific testing including splashing, negating the need to rely on a second flush is definitely something to look out for, so seeing a demonstration of how a toilet flushes is a great place to start.

How are Rimless Toilets Installed?

Rimless toilets are installed in the same way as traditional toilets, though steps may vary depending on manufacturer and design. This means no extra stresses with the added comfort of a superior flush.
